summary.text: A 17-year-old female presented in August 2023 with 1 week of non-bloody diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, decreased appetite and fatigue, with an 8-pound weight loss. She was not hypertensive or edematous. Initial laboratory evaluation showed acute kidney injury with creatinine 2.82 mg/dL and abnormal urinalysis; despite IV fluids creatinine rose to 4.06 mg/dL with edema and oliguria, and inflammatory markers and ANA were abnormal.

Renal biopsy showed crescentic glomerulonephritis, with final pathology of cellular crescents in 47 of 50 glomeruli, fibrinoid necrosis and linear IgG and C3 GBM staining. Anti-GBM antibodies were 115 AU/mL and anti-MPO antibodies 67 AU/mL, chest CT showed no pulmonary involvement, and rheumatology found left knee arthritis. A presumptive diagnosis of anti-GBM disease was made.

She received IV methylprednisolone pulses, 5 plasma exchange sessions, three doses of cyclophosphamide with dose adjustments, prednisone and rituximab. Hemodialysis was started 1 week after presentation. Complications included desaturation with facial rash during transfusion, severe neutropenia treated with filgrastim, a yeast infection treated with fluconazole, weight loss with vomiting and malnutrition improved with mirtazapine, and recurrent pericalcific arthritis treated with steroids.

Antibodies normalized with induction and renal recovery was not attained; she remained dependent on hemodialysis with transplant anticipated. At the most recent pediatric rheumatology visit she was clinically inactive with a BVAS of 0 and undetectable antibodies, and she transitioned to adult rheumatology, where latent tuberculosis was diagnosed and treated with 6 months of isoniazid.

Levels of anti-GBM and anti-MPO antibodies beginning from presentation. The solid arrows represent PLEX, dotted arrows cyclophosphamide doses, and arrowheads rituximab doses. Both anti-GBM and anti-MPO antibody levels have remained 0 since week 28. GBM, glomerular basement membrane; MPO, myeloperoxidase; PLEX, plasma exchange.

article_limitations: Figure panels were pixel-inspected in the separate visual submission; the annotation figures keep caption-level status not_inspected.
Values printed inside Fig. 2 (treatment doses and weeks) and Fig. 4 (antibody curves) are pixel content and are not copied into facts.
The GBM thickening degree on electron microscopy differs between the case text and the Fig. 1 caption; both are review-only.
Most workup and treatment steps carry no stated times; only explicitly scoped times are recorded.
Table 1 rows other than the current-study row are published cases, not patients of this article.
No supplements are listed in the source.
Hemodialysis start: case text "1 week after presentation" kept; discussion "dialysis dependence at presentation" treated as loose wording (review-only ambiguity).
Fig. 4 shows two solid PLEX arrows against 5 PLEX sessions in the text; recorded as a figure limitation.
Fig. 2 caption footnote week numbers have no stated week-0 reference.
